import sqlite3

CONNECTION = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
CONNECTION.execute('CREATE TABLE orders (customer TEXT, items TEXT)')


def save(order):
    cursor = CONNECTION.execute('INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?)', (order['customer'], ','.join(order['items'])))
    return cursor.lastrowid

# Architecture

Orders come in through the API, the core checks them, and the store saves them.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  api[api/handlers.py] --> core[core/orders.py] --> store[store/db.py]
```

- [api/handlers.py](../api/handlers.py) takes the request.
- [core/orders.py](../core/orders.py) holds the rules: an order needs an item.
- [store/db.py](../store/db.py) saves the order in SQLite, in memory.
